assertions.description: HTMLCameraElement exists and the parser constructs it for <camera> (not HTMLUnknownElement).
HTMLMicrophoneElement exists and the parser constructs it for <microphone>.
Both elements expose the single-track surface: a track property and an ontrack event handler.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof HTMLCameraElement === 'undefined' || typeof HTMLMicrophoneElement === 'undefined') return false; const c = document.createElement('camera'), m = document.createElement('microphone'); return 'track' in c && 'ontrack' in c && 'track' in m && 'ontrack' in m; })()

assertions.description: Both elements expose the capture base: an error property (DOMException or null) plus onerror and oncancel handlers.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof HTMLCameraElement === 'undefined' || typeof HTMLMicrophoneElement === 'undefined') return false; const c = document.createElement('camera'), m = document.createElement('microphone'); return ['error','onerror','oncancel'].every((k) => k in c && k in m) && c.error === null; })()

assertions.description: setConstraints() exists on both elements and accepts a plain MediaTrackConstraintSet (and an omitted argument) without throwing.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof HTMLCameraElement === 'undefined') return false; const c = document.createElement('camera'), m = document.createElement('microphone'); if (typeof c.setConstraints !== 'function' || typeof m.setConstraints !== 'function') return false; try { c.setConstraints({ width: 640, height: 480 }); m.setConstraints({ echoCancellation: true }); c.setConstraints(); return true; } catch (e) { return false; } })()

assertions.description: The single-capability elements expose a track, never a stream: stream/onstream (the <usermedia> surface) are absent from <camera>.
assertions.test: (()=>{ if (typeof HTMLCameraElement === 'undefined') return false; const c = document.createElement('camera'); return 'track' in c && !('stream' in c) && !('onstream' in c); })()

assertions.description: The constraint vocabulary the elements consume is queryable: getSupportedConstraints() reports the core video (width, height, frameRate) and audio (echoCancellation) constrainable properties.
